item.title: The Twilight Zone: Alternate Dimensions and Parallel Worlds — Thu Nov 5, 10:30 AM — Montclair Main - Auditorium
item.description:
This is a paid Adult School class. Click here to register.
The Twilight Zone is known to take its viewers to strange, new worlds. This season is no different with stories about recurring dreams, surreal dreamscapes, co-existing twin strangers as well as alien realms accessible through an unexpected portal or by way of intergalactic space travel.
During our interactive study of alternate dimensions and parallel worlds, we will be passengers on various journeys with reluctant dreamers, haunting doppelgangers and those who must escape an alternate universe or who have a desire to travel back to the comfort of their place on Earth. Join me as we take these unique, unpredictable trips through The Twilight Zone.
Source: Libcal Bccls 10306

item.description:

How you use the library today
What you love about our programs, collections, and spaces

item.title: Theater League of Clifton Announces Auditions for “1776” — Tue Nov 10, 7:00 PM — NJ
item.description: The Theater League of Clifton will hold auditions for its upcoming production of “1776” on Tuesday, September 15; Wednesday, September 16; and Thursday, September 17, from 7:00 p.m. to 9:00 p.m. Callbacks by invitation may also be held Thursday, September 17. Auditions will be held at Living Hope, 303 Maplewood Ave., Clifton, NJ 07013. Performances will be held November 13, 14 and 15 at the Wayne Community Center, 1 Pike Drive, Wayne, NJ. The production will be directed by Maren Sugarman. With music and lyrics by Sherman Edwards and a book by Peter Stone, 1776 dramatizes the struggle within the Second Continental Congress to declare American independence. John Adams, Benjamin Franklin and Thomas Jefferson attempt to persuade a divided Congress to break with England while political, regional and personal conflicts threaten to derail the effort. item.title: 5 Week Course: The Work on Inadequacy (Timing Option A) Price - Sliding Scale — Sat Nov 14, 9:00 AM
item.description:
The Mindful Stream To celebrate 5 years of The Work Runs Free, Emrys has created The Work on Inadequacy. Over 5 weeks, we explore different ways the experience of inadequacy shows up in our lives, using The Work to investigate our experience.
Sign up form: [Click Here](https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSeQVso7QaCu9ubv5E_74f50c6vvp2nt7zx8zMWnlGkwaNIYMw/viewform?usp=preview) Detailed Course Outline: [Click Here](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1eQYHU2jgRlNoO_XZDEjj08EhT8jeHk0h2zAOnEoglgM/edit?usp=sharing)
**Sliding Scale Price:** $120 — Accessible rate / $150 — Standard rate / $180 — Pay it forward
**Week 1 — I'm Not Good Enough:** The fundamental inadequacy story. **Week 2 — Comparison:** Measuring ourselves against other people. **Week 3 — I'm a Fraud / They'll Find Me Out:** Imposter feelings, competence and exposure. **Week 4 — Being Loved, Accepted & Enough:** Inadequacy in relationships, belonging and being seen by others. **Week 5 — Achievement & Where I Should Be:**

item.title: Youth Mental Health First Aid Training for ADULTS - November 2026 — Wed Nov 18, 12:00 PM — Virtual
item.description:
Youth Mental Health First Aid is designed for adults who regularly interact with young people ages 12–18. It teaches parents, caregivers, family members, teachers, school staff, and other caring adults how to recognize and respond to mental health or substance use challenges and support a young person who may be experiencing a crisis. The Course will:
Introduce common mental health challenges for youth Review typical adolescent development Teach a 5-step action plan for how to help young people in both crisis and non-crisis situations
Participants will receive certification after completion of all pre and post work, as well as 4 live virtual training sessions. Registration closes 11/10.
Source: MHA of Essex and Morris

item.title: Weekend Warrior Tennis (Sundays) — Sun Nov 22, 9:00 AM
item.description:
North Jersey Bowling, Volleyball, Tennis & More Join us for friendly and sociable free rallies and possibly some informal matches for training and fun. We are beginner to intermediate levels but all are welcome. We don’t allow formal instruction on our group-reserved courts, although giving some quick tips is OK so long as you’re not holding up others waiting to play.
⛑️ **Clinic Matches:** If we have to rotate people in then we may play some clinic-style matches where everyone rotates in evenly. There is no holding the court via wins so everyone has a chance to play regardless of skill level.
🕊️ **Early Bird Start:** If you want to meet earlier than 9 AM (like 8 or 8:30) then please let us know by the day before and we’ll see who can join you (usually I can do earlier).
**🎾 Equipment:** Please bring your own racquet and water, as we don’t provide those. I always have some balls for at least one court, but feel free to bring your own in case we need to branch out over more than one

item.title: Library Speakers Consortium - Middle School Mayhem and Laugh-Out-Loud Misadventures with Jeff Kinney — Thu Jan 7, 4:00 PM — Nutley Free Public Library
item.description:
You must register here to attend: https://libraryc.org/nutleypubliclibrary/229622
Join us online for a hilarious, action-packed virtual conversation with #1 international bestselling author Jeff Kinney as he introduces the 21st book in his globally beloved series, Diary of a Wimpy Kid: Fight or Flight.
Greg Heffley is about to learn that surviving middle school is no easy feat.
In Fight or Flight, Greg’s hard-earned expertise on navigating the rough-and-tumble world of middle school is put to the test.
When a secret binder filled with Greg’s notes on the school’s biggest bullies falls into the wrong hands, his world quickly begins to unravel. Now it’s a race against time before the truth comes out. Will Greg throw in the towel—or go down swinging?
Complete with Kinney's signature comic illustrations and sharp, laugh-out-loud humor, this latest installment captures the awkward, unpredictable realities of growing up that have made Greg Heffley an icon for generations of readers.

item.description:

item.title: Library Speakers Consortium - Harnessing Joy Through Life's Great Labors: A Conversation with Doula and Storyteller Brandi Sellerz-Jackson — Tue Jan 19, 2:00 PM — Nutley Free Public Library
item.description:
You must register here to attend: https://libraryc.org/nutleypubliclibrary/259704
Join us in virtual conversation with Brandi Sellerz-Jackson as she talks about her book, On Thriving: Harnessing Joy Through Life’s Great Labors, a moving guide to self-awareness and radical joy that Ms. magazine praised for taking readers beyond survival into presence and pleasure.
Drawing from her experiences as a doula and intimate storytelling from her own life, Sellerz-Jackson guides us through the many phases of these great labors—labors that we can get stuck in, stunting our ability to thrive. Across age, gender, economic status, or background, we all move through the great labor of our relationships, our mental health, grief and loss, and the feeling of being othered. Sellerz-Jackson doesn’t shy away from the pitfalls of these labors but rather challenges us to actively remain present within them and ask ourselves: What do I need to thrive in the space I’m currently in?
